## Overview

This project packages **four modern fine-tuning techniques** into **two runnable local pipelines** on a consumer NVIDIA GPU. You download a base language model, train small **adapter layers** on your machine, then chat with the result in a **Gradio web UI** — no cloud API required.

| Project | Model | Method | Best for |
|---------|-------|--------|----------|
| **1 — Speed Run** | Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | **QLoRA + Unsloth** | Domain format, instructions, corporate knowledge |
| **2 — Preference Align** | Qwen2.5-1.5B / 7B-Instruct | **ORPO + DoRA** | Tone, style, chosen vs rejected responses |

**GitHub:** [sophalchan/modern-llm-finetuning-lab](https://github.com/sophalchan/modern-llm-finetuning-lab)

**Stack:** PyTorch · PEFT · TRL · bitsandbytes · Gradio · Hugging Face

::: {.callout-note}
**Results & testing:** Training benchmarks, sample outputs, and GPU metrics will be published in a **separate follow-up article**. This page covers project structure, architecture, and how to run the lab.
:::

## What it does (plain English)

A base model like **Qwen2.5-1.5B** already knows general language. This lab **teaches it your preferred style** by showing pairs of good vs bad answers during training (**ORPO**), using efficient adapter updates (**DoRA**), and loading the model in **4-bit** so it fits an **8 GB GPU**.

After training you get a small folder (`orpo_qwen_final/`, ~40 MB) — your custom layer on top of the base model. The **Web UI** lets you chat in a browser at `http://localhost:7860` without typing terminal commands.

## The 4 techniques (simple definitions)

| Technique | What it does |
|-----------|----------------|
| **QLoRA** | Keeps the big model in 4-bit; trains only tiny adapter layers → fits on one GPU |
| **Unsloth** | Optimized training kernels → 2–5× faster (Project 1) |
| **ORPO** | Aligns preferences in **one step** — no separate SFT then DPO |
| **DoRA** | Weight-decomposed LoRA — updates direction and magnitude separately for better quality |

## Background of the Study

Full fine-tuning of 7B–8B models on a laptop GPU is impractical. The industry moved to **parameter-efficient** methods: train adapters, not every weight. **QLoRA** made 8B models reachable on 16 GB cards; **Unsloth** made training fast enough for iteration; **ORPO** simplified preference alignment; **DoRA** improved adapter quality without full-parameter cost.

This lab turns those ideas into **copy-paste scripts** with YAML configs — runnable on Linux + NVIDIA CUDA.

## Motivation of the Study

- **Run locally** on consumer hardware instead of cloud-only fine-tuning
- **Compare two real use cases:** domain instruction tuning vs preference alignment
- **Use community-standard tools** (Unsloth, TRL ORPO, PEFT DoRA)
- **Ship a Web UI** for portfolio demos and interviews
- **Document GPU requirements honestly** — 8 GB works for Project 2 with the low-VRAM config

## Project structure

```text
modern-llm-finetuning-lab/
│
├── configs/
│   ├── project1_unsloth_qlora.yaml   ← Llama 8B + Unsloth settings
│   ├── project1_low_vram.yaml
│   ├── project2_orpo_dora.yaml       ← Qwen 7B ORPO settings
│   └── project2_low_vram.yaml        ← Qwen 1.5B for 8 GB GPU
│
├── project1_unsloth_qlora/
│   ├── train_llama31_unsloth.py      ← Project 1: train
│   ├── infer_llama31_unsloth.py      ← Project 1: terminal inference
│   └── export_gguf.py                ← Export for Ollama / LM Studio
│
├── project2_orpo_dora/
│   ├── train_qwen_orpo.py            ← Project 2: ORPO + DoRA train
│   └── infer_qwen_orpo.py            ← Project 2: terminal inference
│
├── src/
│   ├── inference_engine.py           ← Shared model loader (CLI + UI)
│   └── utils.py                      ← GPU check, YAML loader, HF token
│
├── app_ui.py                         ← Gradio Web UI (port 7860)
├── scripts/
│   ├── install.sh                    ← One-command setup (Python 3.11)
│   ├── run_ui.sh                     ← Start Web UI
│   └── check_environment.py          ← Verify CUDA + packages
│
├── orpo_qwen_final/                  ← Trained adapters (after Project 2)
│   ├── adapter_config.json
│   └── adapter weights (~40 MB)
│
├── requirements-base.txt
├── .env.example                      ← Optional HF_TOKEN
└── README.md
```

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `configs/*.yaml` | Hyperparameters — model, steps, learning rate, output folder |
| `train_qwen_orpo.py` | Loads base model in 4-bit, runs ORPOTrainer, saves adapters |
| `inference_engine.py` | Loads base + adapters once; generates answers for CLI and UI |
| `app_ui.py` | Browser chat — temperature, max tokens, example prompts |
| `orpo_qwen_final/` | Your trained adapter checkpoint |

**Three layers to remember:** Config (recipe) → Train/infer scripts (work) → UI + engine (talk to the model).

### What the Web UI status line means

When you see:

> **Status: Ready — Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (ORPO + DoRA)**

| Part | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Ready** | CUDA GPU found, adapters loaded, model can answer |
| **Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct** | Base model (fits 8 GB VRAM in 4-bit) |
| **ORPO + DoRA** | Trained with preference alignment and DoRA adapters |

## How each part works (step by step)

### Step 1 — Config (`configs/project2_low_vram.yaml`)

The training recipe for an **8 GB GPU**:

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `model_id` | Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Small enough for 8 GB VRAM |
| `use_dora: true` | DoRA enabled | Better adapter quality |
| `max_steps: 10` | Short demo run | Proves pipeline works quickly |
| `output_dir` | orpo_qwen_final | Where adapters are saved |

Increase `max_steps` and `train_samples` for production-quality training (covered in the results article).

### Step 2 — Training (`project2_orpo_dora/train_qwen_orpo.py`)

1. Load Qwen base model in **4-bit** (bitsandbytes)
2. Attach **DoRA** adapter layers (PEFT)
3. Load preference dataset — each row has a question, a **chosen** answer, and a **rejected** answer
4. **ORPOTrainer** teaches the model to prefer chosen over rejected
5. Save adapters to `orpo_qwen_final/`

### Step 3 — Inference engine (`src/inference_engine.py`)

Shared by the **terminal CLI** and **Web UI**:

1. Read `orpo_qwen_final/adapter_config.json` (base model name, DoRA flag)
2. Load base Qwen in 4-bit on GPU
3. Attach saved PEFT adapters
4. `generate()` — format question as chat, run `model.generate()`, return assistant text

The engine loads **once** and reuses the model for every question (faster after the first reply).

### Step 4 — Web UI (`app_ui.py`)

Gradio chat interface on port **7860**:

- **Status bar** — model name and method
- **Temperature slider** — 0 = more factual, 1 = more creative
- **Max tokens slider** — controls answer length
- **Chat window** — conversation history
- **Example prompts** — one-click test questions

## Step-by-step — run locally

### Step 1 — Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sophalchan/modern-llm-finetuning-lab.git
cd modern-llm-finetuning-lab
bash scripts/install.sh
source .venv/bin/activate
python scripts/check_environment.py
```

Requires **Linux**, **NVIDIA GPU**, **Python 3.11**, and CUDA PyTorch.

### Step 2 — Train Project 2 (ORPO + DoRA)

```bash
python project2_orpo_dora/train_qwen_orpo.py --config project2_low_vram.yaml
```

Creates `orpo_qwen_final/` with your trained adapters.

### Step 3 — Terminal inference (optional)

```bash
python project2_orpo_dora/infer_qwen_orpo.py --prompt "What is ORPO fine-tuning?"
```

### Step 4 — Launch the Web UI

```bash
pip install gradio
python app_ui.py
```

Open **http://localhost:7860** — chat with your fine-tuned model in the browser.

Or use the shortcut:

```bash
bash scripts/run_ui.sh
```

### Step 5 — Project 1 (optional, 16 GB+ VRAM)

```bash
pip install "unsloth[colab-new] @ git+https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth.git"
python project1_unsloth_qlora/train_llama31_unsloth.py
python project1_unsloth_qlora/infer_llama31_unsloth.py
python project1_unsloth_qlora/export_gguf.py   # Ollama / LM Studio
```

Set `HF_TOKEN` in `.env` for gated models (Llama 3.1).

## Advantages of this project

| Advantage | Why it matters |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Runs locally** | No API keys, no cloud cost, data stays on your machine |
| **8 GB GPU works** | 1.5B + 4-bit + low_vram config fits consumer laptops |
| **ORPO in one step** | No separate SFT then DPO pipeline |
| **DoRA quality** | Better than plain LoRA for preference tuning |
| **Web UI included** | Easy demo for portfolio and interviews |
| **Shared inference code** | Same engine for CLI and UI |
| **YAML configs** | Change model or steps without editing Python |
| **Two projects in one repo** | Compare speed-run SFT vs preference alignment |

## Hardware note

| Requirement | Detail |
|-------------|--------|
| GPU | NVIDIA — **8 GB** works (Project 2 + `project2_low_vram.yaml`); **16 GB+** for Llama 8B / Qwen 7B |
| OS | Linux + CUDA |
| Python | **3.11** recommended (3.14 breaks some packages) |
| Disk | ~20 GB+ for model weight cache |

## Limitations

- Demo config uses **10 training steps** — enough to prove the pipeline; production needs thousands of steps
- **Project 1 (Unsloth)** needs more VRAM and may have package conflicts on some setups
- Web UI runs **locally only** — not hosted on GitHub Pages (needs your GPU)
- Preference data is a public Hugging Face sample — swap in your own dataset for domain-specific alignment
